summary: VS-019 research compendium (shared with VS-017) provides comprehensive analysis of streaming deterministic 5.76km² sandbox biomes around the player. Document covers chunk streaming, biome systems, FastNoiseLite integration, and performance optimization with 300+ links.

strengths.description: Comprehensive research with 300+ curated links covering biome systems, deterministic generation, streaming patterns, and Godot 4.6 PCG3D features.
Detailed FastNoiseLite biome distribution analysis with specific implementation details for beach, forest, meadow, hills, fauna, houses, and river/mountain boundaries.
Complete chunk lifecycle documentation (queueing, building, spawning, disposal) with performance budget recommendations.
Clear deterministic seeding strategy using hash() of world_id + chunk_coords + version string for reproducible world generation.
Extensive code samples including complete chunk class, procedural river system, noise-based terrain generation, and child-safe prop selection.
Comprehensive performance section with budget tracking (3.5ms/frame), LOD strategies, visibility culling, and memory management.
Complete testing framework for determinism, performance, and boundary conditions of the streaming world system.

suggestions.description: Consider documenting a step-by-step migration from current custom streaming to Godot 4.6 native PCG3D for future maintainability.
Add a quick-reference cheat sheet at the beginning for common streaming patterns and constants.

notes: VS-019 shares the research document with VS-017, which is appropriate as they are closely related (streaming biomes vs scaling island).
The document provides complete implementation guidance for streaming biomes around the player with deterministic generation.
Acceptance criteria for biome continuation (forest, beach, meadow, hills, fauna, houses, collisions, river and mountain boundary) are explicitly addressed.
The existing world_renderer.gd already implements the chunk-based streaming system with appropriate constants.
300+ external links provide extensive resources for implementation.

decision.reason: Comprehensive research document meets all VS-019 acceptance criteria with extensive code samples, performance analysis, and testing strategies. Ready for integration.
